paragraphs: Mar Zutra the Pious. When they carried him on shoulders, he said, “For power is not forever”: Sanhedrin chapter 1. When he placed a Torah scholar under a ban, he first placed himself under a ban: Moed Katan 17a; Nedarim chapter 1, 7b. His silver cup was stolen. He saw a scholar wiping with his fellow’s garment and said, “This is the thief.” He bound him, and he confessed: Bava Metzia 24a.
